/-!
# Erdős Problem 44: Extending Sidon Sets

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/44](https://www.erdosproblems.com/44)
-/

open Function Set Finset

namespace Erdos44

-- Reference: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2103.15850
/-- The maximum size of a Sidon set in `{1, ..., N}` is less than or equal to `2 * √N`. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 5 11]
theorem maxSidonSubsetCard_icc_bound (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    maxSidonSubsetCard (Icc 1 N) ≤ 2 * Real.sqrt N := by
  have key : maxSidonSubsetCard (Finset.Icc 1 N) ^ 2 ≤ 4 * N := by
    -- Pick a Sidon subset of `{1, ..., N}` of maximal size.
    obtain ⟨B, hB, hBeq⟩ := Finset.exists_mem_eq_sup
      ((Finset.Icc 1 N).powerset.filter fun B : Finset ℕ ↦ IsSidon (B : Set ℕ))
      ⟨∅, by simp [IsSidon]⟩ Finset.card
    rw [maxSidonSubsetCard, hBeq]
    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_powerset] at hB
    obtain ⟨hsub, hsid⟩ := hB
    -- Distinct ordered pairs of elements of `B` have distinct differences, and each difference
    -- lies in `{-N, ..., N}`.
    have hcard : B.offDiag.card ≤ (Finset.Icc (-(N : ℤ)) N).card := by
      refine Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn (fun p ↦ (p.1 : ℤ) - p.2) ?_ ?_
      · rintro ⟨a, b⟩ hab
        rw [Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_offDiag] at hab
        have ha' := Finset.mem_Icc.mp (hsub hab.1)
        have hb' := Finset.mem_Icc.mp (hsub hab.2.1)
        simp only [Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_Icc]
        omega
      · rintro ⟨a, b⟩ ha ⟨c, d⟩ hc hac
        rw [Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_offDiag] at ha hc
        simp only at hac
        have hsum : a + d = c + b := by omega
        rcases hsid a ha.1 c hc.1 d hc.2.1 b ha.2.1 hsum with ⟨h1, h2⟩ | ⟨h1, h2⟩
        · simp [h1, h2]
        · exact absurd h1 ha.2.2
    have hIcc : (Finset.Icc (-(N : ℤ)) N).card = 2 * N + 1 := by
      rw [Int.card_Icc]
      omega
    rw [Finset.offDiag_card, hIcc] at hcard
    have hle : B.card ≤ N := by simpa using Finset.card_le_card hsub
    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos B.card with h0 | hpos
    · simp [h0]
    have hkk : B.card ≤ B.card * B.card := Nat.le_mul_of_pos_left _ hpos
    calc B.card ^ 2 = B.card * B.card := sq B.card
      _ ≤ 2 * N + 1 + B.card := by omega
      _ ≤ 4 * N := by omega
  have h1 : ((maxSidonSubsetCard (Finset.Icc 1 N) : ℝ)) ^ 2 ≤ 4 * N := by exact_mod_cast key
  have h2 : (2 : ℝ) * Real.sqrt N = Real.sqrt (4 * N) := by
    rw [show (4 : ℝ) * N = 2 ^ 2 * N by ring, Real.sqrt_mul (by positivity),
      Real.sqrt_sq (by norm_num)]
  rw [h2, ← Real.sqrt_sq (by positivity : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (maxSidonSubsetCard (Finset.Icc 1 N) : ℝ))]
  exact Real.sqrt_le_sqrt h1

/--
**Erdős Problem 44:** Let N ≥ 1 and `A ⊆ {1,…,N}` be a Sidon set. Is it true that, for any ε > 0,
there exist M = M(ε) and `B ⊆ {N+1,…,M}` such that `A ∪ B ⊆ {1,…,M}` is a Sidon set
of size at least `(1−ε)M^{1/2}`?

This problem asks whether any Sidon set can be extended to achieve a density
arbitrarily close to the optimal density for Sidon sets.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_44 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (N ≥ (1 : ℕ)) (A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N), IsSidon (A : Set ℕ) →
    ∀ᵉ (ε > (0 : ℝ)), ∃ᵉ (M > N) (B ⊆ Finset.Icc (N + 1) M),
      IsSidon (A ∪ B : Set ℕ) ∧ (1 - ε) * Real.sqrt M ≤ (A ∪ B).card := by
  sorry

/--
The case where we start with an empty set (constructing large Sidon sets).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_44.variants.empty_start : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (ε > (0 : ℝ)), ∀ᶠ (M : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
    ∃ᵉ (A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 M), IsSidon (A : Set ℕ) ∧ (1 - ε) * Real.sqrt M ≤ A.card := by
  sorry

/-  ## Related results and examples -/

/--
The set `{1, 2, 4, 8, 13}` is a Sidon set in `{1, ..., 13}`.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 5 11]
theorem example_sidon_set : IsSidon ({1, 2, 4, 8, 13} : Set ℕ) := by
  intro i₁ hi₁ j₁ hj₁ i₂ hi₂ j₂ hj₂ hsum
  simp only [Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hi₁ hj₁ hi₂ hj₂
  rcases hi₁ with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
  rcases hj₁ with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
  rcases hi₂ with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
  rcases hj₂ with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
  simp_all

/--
For any `N`, there exists a Sidon set of size at least `√N/2`.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 5 11]
theorem sidon_set_lower_bound (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    ∃ᵉ (A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N), IsSidon (A : Set ℕ) ∧ N.sqrt / 2 ≤ A.card := by
  sorry

/--
The greedy construction gives a Sidon set of size approximately `√N`.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 5 11]
theorem greedy_sidon_construction (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    ∃ᵉ (A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N), IsSidon (A : Set ℕ) ∧ A.card ≥ N.sqrt := by
  sorry

end Erdos44

findings.description: Line 127 asserts an all-N square-root lower bound: some Sidon subset of {1,…,N} has cardinality at least ⌊√N⌋. This is not the elementary greedy bound given in the cited paper, which has exponent 1/3, not 1/2. The existential statement also does not constrain A to be greedy, so it states a different extremal existence result rather than establishing the claimed property of the greedy construction. Lean computation confirms that the greedy sequence has only 17 terms at most 324, with the next term 361, whereas Nat.sqrt 324 = 18. This computation refutes the greedy interpretation, not the unconstrained existential theorem itself.
findings.source_evidence: Balogh–Füredi–Roy, “An upper bound on the size of Sidon sets,” arXiv:2103.15850v2, §1: “Erdős immediately observed that the greedy algorithm gives S(n) ≥ n^{1/3}.” The independent problem statement at https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/340 likewise gives the elementary N^{1/3} lower bound and asks about growth at least N^{1/2−ε}.
findings.suggested_fix: State the cited cube-root bound, for example `∃ᵉ (A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N), IsSidon (A : Set ℕ) ∧ N ≤ A.card ^ 3`, and correct the docstring to exponent 1/3. If a square-root extremal existence theorem is intended instead, supply a separate source and do not attribute it to the greedy construction.

findings.description: The docstring says “size at least √N/2,” but both `N.sqrt` and `/ 2` in line 119 operate in ℕ. The formal lower bound is therefore ⌊√N/2⌋, not the real number √N/2. For example, N = 9 and A = {1} satisfy the formal witness conditions, although 3/2 ≤ |A| is false; at N = 1 even the empty set satisfies the formal conditions. These discrepancies were verified in Lean. The rounded theorem is a valid weaker lower bound, but its docstring does not describe it exactly.
findings.source_evidence: 44.lean, lines 114–119, supplies the explicit “at least √N/2” wording; this auxiliary bound has no individual external citation. The cited paper arXiv:2103.15850v2, Appendix, constructs a q-element Bose–Chowla Sidon set in {1,…,q²−1} for prime powers q. Taking q to be an appropriate power of two yields the unrounded √N/2 lower bound, with N = 1,2 handled by a singleton.
findings.suggested_fix: To match the documented bound, replace the inequality by `Real.sqrt (N : ℝ) / 2 ≤ (A.card : ℝ)`. Alternatively, explicitly document the rounded lower bound if that weaker corollary is intended.

status_issues.source_status: The affirmative assertion is a classical solved result: the maximum cardinality S(M) of a Sidon subset of {1,…,M} satisfies S(M) = (1 + o(1))√M. In particular, for every ε > 0 the stated lower bound holds for every sufficiently large M.
status_issues.evidence: arXiv:2103.15850v2, §6, Theorem 6.1 explicitly states S_ℓ(n) = (1 + o(1))√(ℓn), and the preceding text says ℓ = 1 corresponds exactly to Sidon sets. §6.2 and the Appendix explain the finite-field lower-bound construction.
status_issues.suggested_change: Change the category to `research solved` (or `textbook` if treated as a classical building block) and replace `answer(sorry)` with `answer(True)`. Cite the classical asymptotic result.

reformulations.difference: The source explicitly requires A ∪ B ⊆ {1,…,M} without explicitly writing M > N. Lean instead requires M > N and omits that containment.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The omitted containment follows immediately from the two interval-subset hypotheses and M > N. Conversely, even interpreting the source literally without any lower bound on M, first enlarge A by x = 2N + 1. This remains Sidon because x exceeds twice every original element. Apply the source assertion to A ∪ {x} with initial cutoff x. Its containment condition forces M ≥ x > N. Use {x} ∪ B as the extension of the original A; the resulting Sidon set and cardinality are unchanged. Thus the universally quantified statements are equivalent. This exact equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean without using the conjecture's sorry proof.
